facts.raw_span: Visual acuity: 20/25 to 20/30 in both eyes (OU)
Few yellow spots present, no pigmentary degeneration
Indistinct grayish circle beyond the arcades
Large, slow scotopic and photopic responses
Complete loss of photoreceptors, ellipsoid zone, and retinal pigment epithelium in superotemporal region
Visual acuity: 20/25 to 20/30 in both eyes (OU)
Few yellow spots present, no pigmentary degeneration
Indistinct grayish circle beyond the arcades
Large, slow scotopic and photopic responses
Complete loss of photoreceptors, ellipsoid zone, and retinal pigment epithelium in superotemporal region

concepts.why: Night blindness since childhood, flat rod electroretinogram, and complete loss of photoreceptors in the superotemporal region are characteristic of retinitis pigmentosa.
Indistinct grayish circle beyond the arcades, superotemporal zones showing hypofluorescence, and clear OCT layers in the central macula suggest choroidal sclerosis.
Visual acuity of 20/25 to 20/30, normal color vision, and inferonasal scotoma are consistent with macular dystrophy.
Night blindness since childhood, normal visual acuity, and flat rod electroretinogram are characteristic of congenital stationary night blindness.
Indistinct grayish circle beyond the arcades, superotemporal zones showing hypofluorescence, and clear OCT layers in the central macula suggest choroidal neovascularization.
Visual acuity of 20/25 to 20/30, normal color vision, and inferonasal scotoma are consistent with optic neuropathy.
Few yellow spots present, flat rod electroretinogram, and complete loss of photoreceptors in the superotemporal region are characteristic of retinal degeneration.
Visual acuity of 20/25 to 20/30, normal color vision, and inferonasal scotoma are consistent with macular hole.
